html:
The Compromise of 1867 divided the Austrian Empire into two states, Austria and Hungary, under one ruler, Franz Joseph, who was emperor of Austria and king of Hungary.

Defeat by Prussia in 1866 had pushed Austria out of Germany and weakened the emperor. To keep the Hungarians loyal after their failed revolution of 1848, he gave Hungary its own parliament and government. The two halves shared only the army, foreign policy and the money to pay for them, and renewed their customs union every ten years.

The deal gave Germans in Austria and Magyars in Hungary the upper hand, while Czechs, Poles, Croats, Romanians and other peoples felt left out. Austria-Hungary lasted until its collapse at the end of the First World War in 1918. See Austria and Hungary.
sum: The Compromise of 1867 divided the Austrian Empire into two states, Austria and Hungary, under one ruler, Franz Joseph, who was emperor of Austria and king of Hungary.
